PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR

Shyam Solanki

Assistant Professor · Plant Pathology · Functional Genomics
Functional Genomics of Plant–Microbe–Soil Interaction

I am an Assistant Professor at South Dakota State University, where I lead research focused on plant–microbe–soil interactions. My research integrates plant immunity, functional genomics, pathogen biology, and beneficial microbiomes to understand and improve crop resilience. I teach “Field Crop Diseases and Management” (PS 433/533, every spring semester) and “Functional Genomics: EVO MPMI” (700 level, alternate spring semesters).

shyam.solanki@sdstate.edu

OUR TEAM

Graduate Students

GRADUATE STUDENT

Sachin Sharma

sachin.sharma@sdstate.edu
Research Bio +

Sachin’s research focuses on soybean genomics and major soilborne pathogens, particularly white mold and Fusarium diseases. His work aims to understand host–pathogen interactions and identify genomic factors that contribute to soybean disease resistance.

GRADUATE STUDENT

Nikhil

nikhil.lnu@sdstate.edu
Research Bio +

Nikhil’s research focuses on the soil microbiome and its practical applications, particularly the discovery of beneficial microbial strains with biostimulant and disease-suppressive potential. His work aims to translate these discoveries into new microbial products for farmers.

GRADUATE STUDENT

Israel Akinlabi

israel.akinlabi@sdstate.edu
Research Bio +

Israel’s research focuses on the evolution of NLR immune receptors, particularly how they acquire additional integrated domains (NLR-IDs). His work examines how these domains contribute to pathogen recognition, specificity, and immune response in the Rpg5 NLR-ID-mediated immune system in barley.

GRADUATE STUDENT

Mrinmoy Sarker

Mrinmoy.Sarker@sdstate.edu
Research Bio +

Mrinmoy’s research focuses on identifying temperature-sensitive motifs in cereal immune receptors and understanding their role in plant defense. His work particularly examines the RMRL-mediated immune system in barley and wheat and how temperature influences innate immune responses.

CT

GRADUATE STUDENT

Chase Tucker

chase.tucker@sdstate.edu
Research Bio +

Chase’s research focuses on Cercospora and other foliar diseases of soybean, along with the evaluation of soybean germplasm for disease response.

SR

INCOMING GRADUATE STUDENT

Sonam Rathore

Sonam.Rathore@sdstate.edu
Research Bio +

Sonam is an incoming graduate student whose research will focus on dsRNA-based approaches for plant disease control, with particular emphasis on soybean soilborne diseases. Her work will explore targeted RNA-based strategies for managing important soybean pathogens and improving disease resistance.
